studies.label: Phase 2: human story creation inspired by persona-generated AI plots

counts_source.locator: PDF pp. 10-11, Section 3.1; random assignment also stated in PDF p. 43, Story writing by participants
counts_source.quote: we recruited 100 human participants using the online platform Proliﬁc ... we analyzed 97 stories: 32 in the control group, 33 in the 1-plot condition, and 32 in the 5-plot condition.

arms.name: 0-plot (control, human only)
arms.description: Write the story without AI plot assistance; participants reporting external AI use were excluded from this arm (PDF p. 11).

arms.name: 1-plot
arms.description: Optional access to one pre-generated plot, randomly drawn from the persona plot pool; requesting and using it were optional (PDF pp. 10-11 and 43).

arms.name: 5-plot
arms.description: Optional access to up to five pre-generated plots, randomly drawn from the persona plot pool; requesting and using them were optional (PDF pp. 10-11 and 43).

studies.task: Write an exactly eight-sentence English story about an adventure on another planet for a teenage and young adult audience (PDF p. 45, task screenshot).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13) on Azure OpenAI generated the plot ideas; ChatGPT o1-preview developed the personas.
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.1: using GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13, temperature = 0.9, top P = 1); model year taken from the explicitly printed version date.

estimates.outcome: Pairwise story similarity: crossed-story mixed model
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine similarity, scaled to 100, between every pair of different stories within the same assigned condition, using OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002. The frequentist mixed model has random intercepts for both story identities in each pair and uses REML (PDF pp. 11 and 13).

regression.model: REML: similarity ~ condition + (1|story1_id) + (1|story2_id); random intercepts for both stories in each pair (PDF p. 13).

sources.quote: The model was estimated using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) on 1,520 pairwise comparisons (496 from the 0-plot condition, 528 from the 1-plot condition, and 496 from the 5-plot condition).

estimates.notes: Arm means are the observed story-average similarities printed in Table S3; they are descriptive levels, not fitted mixed-model arm means. Table 4 reports the fitted baseline and condition effects but no treatment-arm fitted means, which are not reconstructed. The mixed-model uncertainty uses both story identities, each corresponding to one randomized participant, so se_basis is participant although unit is pair. n_units is the full three-arm model count. Its pairwise differences need not equal differences of the descriptive means. Story-average t tests and Cohen’s d are separate records.

open_items: Per-arm randomized counts are not printed. The reported recruitment total and analyzed arm counts are retained without reconstructing assignment counts (PDF pp. 10-11 and 43).
No two-arm participant total is printed for the extracted contrasts. n_total is null rather than summing arm counts; any n_units reported for a regression describes its full three-arm fit.
Table 2 prints unlabeled parenthetical quantities and does not identify the standard-error type. They are not assumed to be SEs; regression.se remains null (PDF p. 12).
Table S3 prints arm means but no SDs for story-average pairwise similarity, and does not state the standardizer for its Cohen’s d values (PDF p. 53).

The Bayesian model’s observation unit and random-effects specification are not printed. Its posterior SDs are not frequentist SEs; its HDIs must not be treated as frequentist confidence intervals or used to derive SEs (PDF pp. 14-15 and 52).
The story-level omnibus ANOVA differs between the main text and Table S3. No correction is inferred, and omnibus statistics are not attached to two-arm contrasts (PDF pp. 13 and 53).

The grouping behind the linguistic results is not explained, and plot-request take-up is not reported. The reconciled screening excludes these contrasts as nonrandomized; no inferred group counts are recorded (PDF pp. 11-12, 15-16 and 43).
The paper names no primary outcome or preregistration. The primary-selection convention is documented in primary_override.
The latest publisher version identified in the citation record is not the PDF provided for extraction; whether it resolves the reporting issues is unverified.

S2_across_people_ai_vs_bau.reason: Use the first-reported all-writer semantic-similarity analysis, the direct centroid replication in Tables 2-3. Among the fixed-idea arms, the larger optional menu offers the greater choice and is closest to the codebook preference for flexible AI access. No pooled AI-arm similarity contrast is reported. The selection does not depend on significance.

S2_across_people_ai_design.reason: Use the same centroid measure for consistency. The larger optional menu is treatment and the single-idea configuration is comparison; the paper does not identify either as a default.

notes: Only the eligible human randomized study is included in studies; screening study IDs are preserved, so it is S2. The full markdown, including references and supplementary materials, was read. All cited quantitative PDF pages were checked with pymupdf.get_text(), with table recovery where useful; image-only opening and task screens were also viewed in memory. The sample is newly recruited; the reprinted Doshi and Hauser column is a different sample. All assistance effects concern offered access. Exclusions for reported outside AI use were confined to the control arm. The centroid, crossed-story mixed-model, story-average, and Bayesian records reuse the same participants and are alternative analyses, not independent samples. Printed signs and numerical precision are preserved; no effect, SE, total count, or arm mean was calculated. Each person produced one analyzed story, so story-score SDs and mixed-model story random effects are at the participant level. Bayesian se_basis is not_reported because its basis is unspecified, despite reported posterior intervals.
